Independent binary reproduction: enumerate RREF subspaces of F_2^6 and test pairwise basis brackets for closure; normalizer codimension is rank of the stacked bracket constraints modulo the subspace. In d=4 restrict enumeration to lifts with projected line.
correctness.rationale: For projection U and central intersection W, the closure condition is wedge^2 U contained in W and the distinct lifts are Hom(U,Z/W). The normalizer projection is the kernel of V -> Hom(U,Z/W), v -> (u -> v wedge u mod W); all central dimensions lie in the normalizer. For a line U, the image of v -> v wedge u is K_U of dimension d-1 with kernel U, so the normalizer codimension is d-1-dim(W intersect K_U). To count W, choose its intersection with K_U and its image in Z/K_U; relative to a splitting the remaining choices are graphs into K_U/(W intersect K_U), giving the stated q power. For d=3, projected planes have 1, q+1, 1 eligible W of dimensions 1, 2, 3 respectively. A vector out of the projected plane gives two independent wedges independent of its wedge line; it normalizes only when W=Z. With the lift factors q^4, q^2, 1 this gives the entire plane contribution. The central, line, and full-projection contributions recover the displayed coefficients, including 577 and 3955 at q=2 and q=3. The proof uses alternating exterior products and is valid in characteristic two. Independent direct bracket tests enumerated all 2825 ambient subspaces of the six-dimensional binary algebra, matching every term and the rank-one strata; a separate binary d=4 rank-one census matched all strata and totaled 395805.
residual_risks: The independent finite diagnostics were over F_2; the proof, not the test cases, establishes arbitrary prime powers. The larger generator-rank formula is only for one-dimensional projection.

value.rationale: Normalizer codimension measures how strongly a subalgebra fails to be an ideal and is not fixed by its dimension or projected rank. A complete census for the first free case beyond the Heisenberg algebra supplies the exact distribution, for instance distinguishing three normalizer codimensions even in the two-dimensional stratum. The rank-one formula extends this natural diagnostic to all finite fields and generator ranks; for odd prime fields normalizer index also has the finite-group interpretation. This is a specific exact invariant useful for comparison of algebra and subgroup censuses, not an arbitrary finite enumeration.
residual_risks: The closed full census stops at three generators and does not classify subalgebra automorphism orbits.
